blocks.title: Physiotherapist is a protected title
blocks.copy: By law, only people registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) can call themselves a physiotherapist. Every clinician at Forbury Physiotherapy is HCPC-registered — you can check any of our team on the HCPC register at hcpc-uk.org.

blocks.title: We're regulated by the HCPC, not the CQC
blocks.copy: Physiotherapy clinics like ours are regulated by the HCPC, which registers and holds individual clinicians to account — not the Care Quality Commission (CQC), which inspects settings such as hospitals and care homes. There's no CQC rating to show you, because a private physiotherapy clinic isn't the kind of service the CQC inspects.

blocks.title: What Chartered membership means
blocks.copy: The Chartered Society of Physiotherapy (CSP) is the professional body for physiotherapists. Some of our clinicians are Chartered members — you'll see it noted next to their name on our Team page. It's a mark of professional membership held by the individual, not something a clinic can claim on its own behalf.

blocks.title: Professional indemnity insurance
blocks.copy: Every clinician here holds professional indemnity insurance, covering you in the unlikely event that something goes wrong with your treatment.

blocks.title: DBS checks
blocks.copy: All clinical staff hold an up-to-date Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check, renewed regularly as part of our safeguarding practice.

blocks.title: Data protection
blocks.copy: We're registered with the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO reference ZA000000 — sample number for demonstration) and handle your health records in line with UK GDPR.

verifyRegisterCopy: You can check any HCPC-registered physiotherapist, including our team, on the HCPC register at hcpc-uk.org — search by name or registration number.
